findings.problem: BatchWorkflow has no typestate enum; status is a free-form String and is_sent/is_validated are independent booleans, so illegal state combinations like status='sent' with is_sent=false or status='new' with is_sent=true are representable
findings.failure_mode: Any consumer cannot rely on the struct to enforce valid lifecycle transitions; downstream logic may branch on strings/booleans that never synchronize with actual workflow state
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single BatchStatus enum whose variants carry owned lifecycle data (e.g., Variant::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }), making every legal state a variant and every illegal state unrepresentable

findings.problem: status is a pub String field; any caller can set status to any string value including typos, empty strings, or values outside the domain vocabulary
findings.failure_mode: Typos or invalid strings silently bypass transition logic; pattern matches on status elsewhere must use string equality rather than exhaustive enum matching, enabling unhandled cases
findings.fix: Replace pub status: String with a private BatchStatus enum field; remove pub access to status entirely; expose state only through enum variants

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that cannot encode a proper state machine; both can be true simultaneously or contradict the status string
findings.failure_mode: Boolean fields create a 4x state space (validated×sent) that is incomprehensible at the call site and cannot prevent contradictions like validated=true, sent=true, status='draft'
findings.fix: Remove both booleans and encode the full lifecycle as a single enum typestate with explicit transitions (e.g., New -> Validated -> Sent)

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is optional lifecycle data stored outside the variant that owns it; it can be None when is_sent=true or Some(...) when status is not sent
findings.failure_mode: A batch marked as sent can have sent_at_epoch_ms=None, and a non-sent batch can carry a stale epoch value, breaking any timestamp-dependent downstream logic
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the BatchStatus::Sent variant as u64 (not Option), so sent batches always have a timestamp and non-sent batches never carry one

findings.problem: id is a pub String; any caller can construct a BatchWorkflow with an empty string, non-UUID text, or any value that violates domain invariants on batch identifiers
findings.failure_mode: No validation is enforced at construction; invalid or collision-prone IDs silently enter the domain, and callers cannot distinguish validated identifiers from raw strings
findings.fix: Introduce a BatchId newtype with a fallible smart constructor (e.g., BatchId::try_from(s: &str) -> Result<BatchId, ParseError>) and store it as a private field

findings.problem: raw primitives String and bool cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct BatchWorkflow directly with any invalid combination of id, status, and booleans
findings.failure_mode: The domain core accepts hostile or inconsistent state from the shell because there is no single constructor that validates all invariants at parse time, so every caller must repeat validation logic
findings.fix: Provide a single BatchWorkflow::try_new(id: &str, initial: BatchStatus) -> Result<Self, ParseError> that validates the id and initializes all lifecycle state from the trusted enum; make all fields private

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates status and is_sent as string/boolean side effects instead of producing a pure domain transition; it returns the mutated struct rather than a Result or a new state value
findings.failure_mode: The command is an imperative shell mutation disguised as a domain function; it can be called on any struct value regardless of current state (no transition guard) and silently overwrites status to 'sent'
findings.fix: Define mark_sent as fn mark_sent(current: &BatchWorkflow) -> Result<BatchWorkflow, TransitionError> that matches on the current BatchStatus variant and returns an error for invalid transitions, or better yet, replace it with a state machine transition method on BatchStatus

findings.problem: mark_sent calls .to_string() on the literal 'sent', allocating a new String every call instead of using a static or enum variant
findings.failure_mode: Every state transition allocates a new heap String even though the status set is finite and known; this violates allocation discipline and adds unmeasured overhead to hot paths
findings.fix: Replace with a static &str comparison or, better, use a BatchStatus enum variant that carries no String allocation

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any hot-path function in this crate
no profiler data to identify or validate the actual bottleneck
no allocation evidence (no alloc counters, no alloc-tracing runs)
no second-ring evidence tied to actual symbols or artifacts
no command-truth evidence: no cargo fmt/check/clippy/test commands documented as run
no workload specification, target hardware description, input distribution, or regression threshold for any performance claim
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate is fundamentally unreviewable at the Holzman level because all domain state is raw primitives with no type-level invariants, no parse boundary, no typed error taxonomy, and no state machine. A complete restructure to enum-based typestate with a single fallible constructor is required before any deeper verification work is meaningful.
